name: VA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 6-point Democratic lean plus a strong national environment for Democrats
Subramanyam's huge fundraising edge ($1.17M raised, $583K on hand vs. $107K)
Prediction markets price the Democrat at 95-97%
First-term incumbent with no serious outside spending against him
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Subramanyam: a D+6 seat, a favorable environment, incumbency, and a roughly 10-to-1 fundraising advantage over Dave Beckwith. Markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price the Democrat near certain, and no polls or ratings suggest any reason to move away from that picture.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Subramanyam or a sharply worse national environment for Democrats would be the main threats to this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Suhas Subramanyam defends a Northern Virginia seat that leans Democratic by about six points, in what fundamentals suggest is a favorable national environment for his party. He has raised $1.17 million and holds $583,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Beckwith has raised about $107,000 with $54,000 available. No outside groups are opposing the incumbent, and an independent candidate trails without visible fundraising.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price the Democrat at 95 to 97 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's lean, the money gap, and incumbency, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic win.
